title: Cap. X Arg. IX: reprobation not a punishment — shown in reprobate angels whom Suarez, Bellarmine, Vasquez say God passed by with no merited penalty in them
pass_a_gloss: But that reprobation or non-election is not a penalty—although the reprobate always fall into everlasting penalties—is plain from the example of the reprobate, or non-elect, Angels, in whom there was nothing that deserved a penalty or torment, and yet God elected certain of them, others he did not elect but passed by, Suarez, Bellarmine, Vasquez confessing it, and all Theologians agreeing.
pass_b_english: That reprobation or non-election is not itself a penalty—though the reprobate always fall into everlasting pains—is plain from the reprobate or non-elect angels: in them there was nothing that deserved penalty or torment, yet God chose some and passed others by. Suarez, Bellarmine, and Vasquez confess it, and the theologians agree.
source_text: Reprobationem autem sive non-electionem non esse poenam; quamvis reprobati semper in poenas incidant sempiternas, patet exemplo Angelorum reprobatorum, sive non-electorum, in quibus nihil erat quod poenam sive supplicium mereretur, et tamen Deus quosdam ex illis elegit, alios non elegit sed praeteriit, fatente Suarez, Bellarmino, Vasquez, ac consentientibus omnibus Theologis.
